plugins.description: Host-level knowledge vault access with zero-config discovery, 3 retrieval tools, and destructive command safety guard for DeepSeek Harness.
plugins.readme_text:
**Give your DeepSeek Harness agent a brain — host-level knowledge access, zero-config vault discovery, and a safety guard for destructive shell commands.** **ต่อสมองให้เอเจนต์ DeepSeek Harness — เข้าถึงคลังความรู้ระดับ host, ค้นหา vault อัตโนมัติแบบไม่ต้องตั้งค่า, และกันคำสั่ง shell ที่ทำลายข้อมูล** [![CI](https://github.com/Babydunx1/dsh-knowledge-bridge/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/Babydunx1/dsh-knowledge-bridge/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE) [![Dependencies: 0](https://img.shields.io/badge/dependencies-0-success.svg)](package.json) [![Tests: 28 passing](https://img.shields.io/badge/tests-28%20passing-brightgreen.svg)](#development) [![Bundle contract: 21 checks](https://img.shields.io/badge/bundle%20contract-21%20checks-blueviolet.svg)](#development) [![Platform: Windows · macOS · Linux](https://img.shields.io/badge/platform-Windows%20%C2%B7%20macOS%20%C2%B7%20Linux-lightgrey.svg)](#installation) **English** · [ภาษาไทย](#-ภาษาไทย)
---
### Architecture at a glance · ภาพรวมสถาปัตยกรรม ```mermaid flowchart LR V[("Knowledge vault
50 items · 229 files")] D["Discovery
env var → ~ → ./"] I["Index
id · title · summary · artifacts"] T["Tools
search · read · list"] A["Agent context"] Q["One-line directive
~140 chars"] G{"Safety guard
exec.name + exec.arguments"} V --> D --> I --> T --> A Q --> A A --> G G -->|"banned pattern"| X["Denied ❌"] G -->|"clean"| R["Executed ✅"] ```
---
### Try it in 10 seconds · ลองใช้ใน 10 วินาที ```bash git clone https://github.com/Babydunx1/dsh-knowledge-bridge && cd dsh-knowledge-bridge npm test # 28 tests — unit + bundle contract, no install needed npm run validate # 21 static checks on the bundle contract npm run demo # index a sample vault and print what the agent would see ``` ```text 2 · index 2 item(s) · 3 artifact(s) ├─ deploy-guide · 1 artifact(s) └─ posttracker_engine · 2 artifact(s) 4 · guard (patterns are matched against the command string) ⛔ BLOCKED git reset --hard HEAD~1 ⛔ BLOCKED rm -rf / ✅ allowed git status ``` No install, no configuration, no DeepSeek Harness required. ไม่ต้องติดตั้ง ไม่ต้องตั้งค่า ไม่ต้องเปิด DeepSeek Harness ก็ลองได้
--- ## 🇬🇧 English ### Why this exists An agent's quality is bounded by what it can *reach*, not by how smart it is. Three concrete failure modes motivated this plugin: 1. **Sandbox false negatives.** Under `workspace-write`, an agent cannot read knowledge vaults or repositories outside the active workspace. On Windows the shell turns that denial into a misleading `File Not Found`, so the agent concludes the knowledge does not exist — and starts guessing. 2. **Context amnesia.** Teams keep 50+ architecture docs, SOPs and API contracts in a vault (Antigravity's `~/.gemini/antigravity-ide/knowledge`, shared drives, `docs/`). DeepSeek Harness has no native way to discover or index them. 3. **Irreversible commands.** Autonomous agents happily run `git reset --hard`, `git clean -fd` or `git restore .` and destroy uncommitted work. `dsh-knowledge-bridge` runs as a **host-level cordis plugin**: it reads the host filesystem with the host process's own permissions, exposes three fast retrieval tools, injects a one-line directive so the model knows a vault exists, and denies destructive shell calls before they execute. ### Goals | Goal | How it is met | |---|---| | **Scoped, on-demand knowledge** | Nothing is dumped into the prompt. One ~140-character directive is injected; content is pulled per topic — `knowledge_search` → `knowledge_read`. | | **Zero configuration** | The vault is auto-discovered from an environment variable or well-known locations. No hardcoded paths anywhere in the code. | | **Zero dependencies** | Node.js built-ins only (`node:fs`, `node:path`, `node:os`). Nothing to install. | | **Never destroy user work** | A monotonic guard: any matching rule denies the call, and no other plugin can force-allow it. | | **Portable** | `~`-relative discovery, `DSH_KNOWLEDGE_PATHS` override, works with any markdown vault layout. | #### What this plugin is *not* - It is **not** a memory system that loads your whole vault into every prompt. A 2 MB vault is ~1M tokens: slow and expensive. - It is **not** a vector database. Ranking is deterministic keyword scoring — predictable, debuggable, no embedding service to run. ### Features | | Feature | Detail | |---|---|---| | 🧠 | `knowledge_search` | Keyword search with explicit weights: title 10 · id 8 · **aliases 8** · **tags 6** · **references 4** · summary 3 · artifact name 2 · **document body 1** (lazy, cached by mtime). Returns `id`, `title`, `score`, a clipped summary and the artifact list — never file content. | | 📖 | `knowledge_read` | Reads a full document, or one specific artifact (`master_guide.md`, `07_migration.md`, …) on demand. | | 🗂️ | `knowledge_list` | The vault outline: ids, titles, artifact counts, one-line previews. | | ℹ️ | `knowledge_info` | Installed version, the exact update command for **this** profile, the restart requirement, and — on demand — whether a newer version is published. The registry lookup never runs at load, and an unreadable registry answers `null`, never a false "up to date". | | 🔎 | Zero-config discovery | `DSH_KNOWLEDGE_PATHS` → `~/.gemini/antigravity-ide/knowledge` → `~/.antigravity-ide/knowledge` → `~/.dsh/knowledge` → `~/.codex/knowledge` → `./knowledge` → `./docs/knowledge` → `./.knowledge`. | | 📜 | Rules injection | Discovers `AGENTS.md` / `GEMINI.md` / `CLAUDE.md` from the workspace and adds them to the system prompt. | | 🛑 | Safety guard | Denies `bash` / `pwsh` / `cmd` / `terminal` calls whose command matches a banned pattern. | | 🪶 | Token-aware | Tool summaries are clipped, because tool output is replayed in every later model call. | ### Installation
Option A — Add plugin: paste the link (recommended, ~1 minute) 1. DeepSeek Harness → **Plugins** → **Add plugin** 2. Paste this address into **Package name or address**: ```text https://github.com/Babydunx1/dsh-knowledge-bridge ``` 3. Click **Install**, then **restart DeepSeek Harness** (a restart loads a fresh JavaScript module generation) Accepted addresses — all of these pass DSH's own check: | Paste this | Kind | |:--|:--| | `https://github.com/Babydunx1/dsh-knowledge-bridge` | Git repository (recommended) | | `github:Babydunx1/dsh-knowledge-bridge` | Git shorthand | | `https://github.com/Babydunx1/dsh-knowledge-bridge#v1.0.0` | Git, pinned to a tag / branch / commit (`#main`, `#semver:^1.0.0`) | | `https://github.com/Babydunx1/dsh-knowledge-bridge/archive/refs/heads/main.tar.gz` | Tarball — use this when Git is not installed on the machine | | `git@github.com:Babydunx1/dsh-knowledge-bridge.git` | Git over SSH | A GitHub **page** URL with extra path segments (e.g. `.../tree/main`) is refused with *"a URL must point at a git repository or a tarball"*. Command-line equivalent (same code path as the dialog): ```bash dsh plugin --profile add https://github.com/Babydunx1/dsh-knowledge-bridge ``` #### 🔁 Updating — just ask your agent DSH has no plugin auto-update yet, and you do not need to learn a command. Tell your agent: > “Update the `dsh-knowledge-bridge` plugin, then tell me what to restart.” The plugin writes the exact command for this profile into the agent's prompt (`knowledge_info` returns it too), so the agent can run it for you. When the host cannot see the profile name, it writes the shell form instead — `$env:DSH_PROFILE` on Windows, `"$DSH_PROFILE"` elsewhere — which the DSH shell resolves for itself: ```bash dsh plugin --profile update dsh-knowledge-bridge # or: Plugins → uninstall → Add plugin again ``` Then **restart DeepSeek Harness** — the new code loads on the n

plugins.description: Tavily-backed WebSearchProvider for the DeepSeek Harness web capability seam (ctx.web) — npm: dsh-tavily-cxykyw
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-tavily-cxykyw

[English](README.md) | [中文](README.zh.md) A [Tavily](https://tavily.com)-backed `WebSearchProvider` for the [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) web capability seam (`ctx.web`). It routes the built-in `web_search` tool to Tavily's dedicated search API instead of the shipped DeepSeek model-based search channel, so **a search costs no model tokens** and the result set comes from a real search engine index rather than an auxiliary model request. Verified against DSH `0.2.0-rc.2`. > Package name note: `dsh-web-search-tavily` on npm belongs to another author. This plugin is published as **`dsh-tavily-cxykyw`**; the GitHub repository is still `cxykyw/dsh-web-search-tavily`. ## What it does - registers a search provider with the stable id **`tavily`** on `ctx.web`; - maps Tavily's response to DSH's normalized `WebSearchResult` — `results[].url/title/content` become `sources[].url/title/snippet`, and Tavily's optional `answer` becomes the result `content`; - resolves the API key on **every** search, in this order: literal `apiKey` → credentials service (`~/.dsh/.credentials.yaml`) → launch environment / `process.env`; - `available()` is a cheap local check (key + base URL present) with no network calls — a missing key surfaces as `WEB_PROVIDER_CREDENTIAL_MISSING` at search time; - then truncates to `request.maxResults` through the seam, exactly like any other provider. ## Install ```sh dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-tavily-cxykyw ``` If your DSH profile is a pnpm workspace root (the default `~/.dsh/profiles/web` is), the add must target the workspace root: ```sh dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-tavily-cxykyw -w ``` The bundled `cordis.patch.yml` declares `dsh.bundle.patch`, so adding the package also registers it as a profile bundle: the provider row is inserted **and** `web.searchProvider` is set to `tavily` for you. Restart `dsh web` afterwards — bundle changes are not hot-reloaded. From a checkout instead of npm: ```sh git clone https://github.com/cxykyw/dsh-web-search-tavily.git dsh plugin --profile web add link:/absolute/path/to/dsh-web-search-tavily -w ``` ## Configure the API key Get a key at [app.tavily.com](https://app.tavily.com) (there is a free tier). Then pick **one** of: **1. Credentials file (recommended — outside every repository):** ```yaml # ~/.dsh/.credentials.yaml TAVILY_API_KEY: tvly-xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx ``` **2. Environment variable** of the process that launches DSH: ```sh TAVILY_API_KEY=tvly-xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx dsh web ``` **3. Literal key in your own profile patch** (works, but keeps the secret in a plain file — prefer 1 or 2): ```yaml # ~/.dsh/profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml - id: web-search-tavily config: apiKey: tvly-xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx ``` > **Never commit an API key.** This repository, its `cordis.patch.yml`, and its published npm tarball contain **no** credentials and no default key: the plugin only ever reads them from your machine at search time. `.gitignore` also excludes `.env*`, `.npmrc`, and `*.local.yml`. ## Options Configurable on the inserted `web-search-tavily` row: | Option | Default | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | `apiKey` | — | Literal Tavily API key. Prefer `apiKeyEnv` + credentials/env. | | `apiKeyEnv` | `TAVILY_API_KEY` | Credential reference / environment variable name to resolve the key from. | | `baseURL` | `https://api.tavily.com` | Tavily API base URL (point it at a proxy if you need one). | | `searchDepth` | `basic` | `basic` (fast, 1 credit) or `advanced` (deeper crawl, more credits). | | `maxResults` | `8` | Results requested per search, 1–20. A per-call `maxResults` still wins. | Example, overriding just the depth and result count: ```yaml # ~/.dsh/profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml - id: web-search-tavily config: searchDepth: advanced maxResults: 5 ``` ## Switching providers The bundle patch already pins the seam: ```yaml - id: web config: searchProvider: tavily fetchProvider: http ``` To fall back to the official DeepSeek search, set `searchProvider: deepseek-official` (or remove the line only if `deepseek-official` is the single usable provider — with two usable providers and no pin, the seam fails closed with `WEB_PROVIDER_AMBIGUOUS`). > Upgrading from a hand-inserted copy in your own profile patch? Delete that `insert` block and keep only the `- id: web-search-tavily` config override above, otherwise the row id is inserted twice. ## Notes and limitations - No Web settings page: DSH `0.2` cannot mount this plugin's settings section, so the provider is configured through the profile patch only. - `fetch` (page retrieval) is untouched — it stays on `@deepseek-ai/dsh-web-fetch-http`. - Tavily search results carry no publication date, so `sources[].publishedAt` is not set. ## Uninstall ```sh dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-tavily-cxykyw -w ``` ## License MIT © cxykyw

plugins.description: 深鲸画布 · DSH 插件：把一段文字变成能发的视频。稿子、素材、成片都在你自己的电脑上，不上传、不联网。免费版可用。
plugins.readme_text:
# 深鲸画布 · DSH 插件

[![Listed on dsh-plugin.org](https://dsh-plugin.org/badges/listed.svg)](https://dsh-plugin.org/plugins/feely0208/dsh-shell-canvas)

把一段文字，变成能发的视频。

贴一段稿子、选几张素材，点一下出横竖双版成片。
**稿子、素材、成片都在你自己的电脑上** —— 不上传、不联网，拔掉网线照样出片。

## 安装

在你所用的、支持 DSH 的载体里打开「插件管理器」，选择**从压缩包安装**，选中下载好的 `.tgz` 即可。

命令行安装：

```bash
# 推荐：从 npm 装（始终取最新版，不钉版本号）
dsh plugin add @deepwhale-cn/dsh-shell-canvas
```

也可以从官网下载插件包后，在插件管理器里「从压缩包安装」：
<https://www.deepwhale.org.cn/download.html>


装完无需重启，界面跟随所在载体的外观。

## 能力

- **一次出三种版式** —— 旁白口播 / 金句引用 / 步骤清单，编排各不相同
- **逐句指定配图** —— 分镜表里逐句安排素材与时长，素材与字幕一一对应
- **一个位置放多张图或一段视频** —— 多图按时间轮播；视频素材会让画面真的动起来
- **每个镜头换版位** —— 尺寸、位置、入场方式逐镜轮换
- **一次出横竖双版** —— 同一份稿子，横版竖版一起给
- **模型不绑任何一家** —— 生图与配音接你自己的接口，密钥留在本机
- **批量出片** —— 一次丢进一整批；一条出错不拖垮整批
- **跨平台** —— macOS / Windows / Linux

## 授权

| | |
|---|---|
| **免费版** | **不限条数**出片，成片带水印，直接下载就能用，不用注册 |
| **授权版** | ¥199/年，去掉水印 + 批量出片 + 每条可查 |

有效期 1 年，期间不限出片次数。授权码按时间到期，**不绑机器**。

## 平台

装在任意支持 DSH 的载体上，**不绑定桌面端**。

plugins.description: DeepSeek Harness (DSH) plugin that publishes the running Harness as a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server for other agent harnesses.
plugins.readme_text:
# DSH MCP Server

[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-yellow.svg)](LICENSE)

A DeepSeek Harness (DSH) plugin that publishes a **Model Context Protocol (MCP)** server from the
running Harness host, so other agent harnesses — Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, another DSH, any MCP
client — can call DSH: start sessions, drive turns, read transcripts, and cancel work.

The plugin is a Host-only bundle with **zero dependencies** (no DSH import, no third-party module),
so it installs into a profile and survives Harness upgrades that keep the service contracts.

```
other harness ──MCP (Streamable HTTP or stdio)──> DSH MCP Server ──> DSH services
                                                                     sessionController / sessionQuery / tools
```

## What it exposes

| MCP tool | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `dsh_run_prompt` | Start a **new** DSH session and run one prompt; returns the assistant's final text and the new `sessionId`. Supports `cwd`, `agentPreset`, `permissionPreset`, `model` (`provider/model`), `wait: false`, `timeoutMs`. |
| `dsh_continue_session` | Send a prompt to an **existing** session (resuming it if it is cold). Keeps the session's context and workspace; `permissionPreset` re-pins the session's sandbox mode and approval policy before the prompt. |
| `dsh_list_commands` | The slash commands a session's agent can currently run: the global command layer plus whatever that agent's preset composes, so availability differs per agent preset. |
| `dsh_run_command` | Run one slash command in a session and return its settled `{ kind, text, commandId }`. `line` takes a complete command line (`"/compact"`, `"/permission danger-full-access"`); `command` (+ optional `args`) takes a bare name. The command executes immediately without a model turn. |
| `dsh_list_sessions` | Visible sessions with title, cwd, running state, archival state, and last activity. Archived sessions are hidden unless `includeArchived: true`, mirroring the Web UI. |
| `dsh_read_session` | Ordered `{ role, text, seq }` transcript of one session (user-authored and assistant messages only), plus the last durable `permissionPreset` when the session has one. Works while the session is archived. |
| `dsh_cancel_session` | Cancel the active turn of a session without dropping its pending inbox. |
| `dsh_archive_session` | Archive one session durably: hidden from every grouping surface, and it cannot run a model step until restored. A session with running work is refused unless `stopActivity: true` (which archives first, then stops that work). Archiving drops the pin. |
| `dsh_unarchive_session` | Drop a session from the archive set; it is listed again and returns to its recorded workspace position. |
| `dsh_list_permission_presets` | The deployment's permission presets (each bundles a sandbox mode with an approval policy) plus the default for new sessions, for the `permissionPreset` argument above. |
| `dsh_list_tools` | The tools DSH exposes to its own agents, for choosing what a delegated prompt can do. |
| `dsh_status` | Endpoint, profile, version, session/live-agent counts, default model, active turns, and the default permission preset. |

Archival needs the Host's `workspaceRegistry` service (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-workspace`). Without it the
two archive tools report that the service is unavailable and listings simply omit the `archived`
field instead of guessing.

Permission presets need the Host's `permissionPresets` service
(`@deepseek-ai/dsh-permission-presets`). `permissionPreset` is applied through that service's own
`set()` — the same write path as the GUI `/permission` command — once the session is live and before
its prompt is admitted, so the turn's own tool calls already see the chosen sandbox mode and approval
policy. The outcome echoes the applied preset; `dsh_read_session` folds the session's last durable
`permission/preset` event back into its payload, and `dsh_status` carries `defaultPermissionPreset`
plus the catalog. Without the service the permission fields are omitted and
`dsh_list_permission_presets` reports that the service is unavailable. A session created without a
`permissionPreset` keeps the deployment default, exactly as a GUI-created session does.

Commands need the Host's `commands` service and are addressed by **agent**, not by session: the
registry merges a global layer with the layers of the preset that agent is mounted under, so
`dsh_list_commands` must be asked per session and a command such as `/compact` exists only when that
session's preset composes it (`standard`/`ptc`/`cordis` do; `minimal` does not). Execution goes
through the same `commands.execute()` the Web composer uses: the handler runs immediately, the
lifecycle is logged as `command/run` + `command/done`, and **no model turn is started**. `kind` is
`success` or `error`; a line the Host would not parse as a command, or a name it does not know, is
rejected with the available commands listed.

Resources: `dsh://status`, `dsh://sessions`, and the template `dsh://session/{sessionId}`.

## Endpoint and authentication

On activation the plugin registers `POST /mcp` on the Harness web server (default
`http://127.0.0.1:19387`) and writes connection details to:

```
$DSH_HOME/mcp/dsh-mcp-endpoint.json      # mode 0600
{ "url": "...", "token": "...", "stdioBridge": "...", "tools": [...] }
```

Every request must present the bearer token:

```
Authorization: Bearer <token>
```

The token is **generated per activation** unless you configure a fixed one. Set a fixed token
whenever another harness keeps a saved config, because a generated token changes on every Harness
restart. In the desktop profile the `dsh-mcp-server` row carries one:

```yaml
- id: dsh-mcp-server
  disabled: false
  config:
    token: "<fixed token>"     # mirrored in the endpoint file and in the selfcheck bundle
```

Requests that already pass DSH's own connection trust (`ctx.connection`) are also accepted, so local
tooling that holds the Harness token works too.

The endpoint file is owned by the activation that wrote it: on a config hot-reload the outgoing
instance removes it only when it is still the owner, so the replacement instance's file is never
deleted mid-reload.

## Configuration

The bundle row in `cordis.patch.yml` accepts (all optional):

| Field | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `path` | `/mcp` | Route path on the Harness web server. |
| `token` | generated | Fixed bearer token; set this so external configs stay stable across restarts. |
| `url` | `$DSH_WEB_URL` or `http://127.0.0.1:19387` | Advertised base URL written to the endpoint file. |
| `endpointFile` | `$DSH_HOME/mcp/dsh-mcp-endpoint.json` | Where connection details are published. |
| `writeEndpointFile` | `true` | Publish the endpoint file at all. |
| `allowConnectionAuth` | `true` | Also accept requests admitted by `ctx.connection`. |
| `defaultCwd` | Harness default | Working directory for sessions started without `cwd`. |
| `defaultModel` | Harness default model | `{ provider, model, reasoningEffort? }` for sessions without an explicit override. |
| `turnTimeoutMs` | `1800000` | Default wait ceiling for a tool call that waits for a turn. |
| `maxConcurrentTurns` | `8` | Concurrent waited turns before new calls queue. |
| `maxBodyBytes` | `8388608` | Request body ceiling. |
| `instructions` | built-in text | Replaces the instructions handed to the calling model. |

Example row:

```yaml
- insert:
    - id: dsh-mcp-server
      name: '@local/dsh-mcp-server'
      config:
        token: !!js process.env.DSH_MCP_TOKEN
        defaultCwd: /Users/me/work
```

## Connecting another harness

### 1. Streamable HTTP (no extra process)

Point the client at the endpoint with the bearer token:

```jsonc
// Claude Code / Cursor style MCP config
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "dsh": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "http://127.0.0.1:19387/mcp",
      "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer <token from dsh-mcp-endpoint.json>" }
    }
  }
}
```

### 2. stdio (harnesses that only spawn a command)

`bin/dsh-mcp-stdio.mjs` is a dependency-free stdio↔HTTP bridge. It discovers the endpoint from
`$DSH_HOME/mcp/dsh-mcp-endpoint.json` (override w

# dsh-flash

> Quick Control panel **core** for the DSH web UI — the floating/docked quick-control panel with an **extensible switch registry** other plugins register their own controls into, the skin system, zh/en i18n and the alert surfaces. The DSH **Workbench** (dock-base) integration ships separately as the `dock-flash` adapter.

**[中文文档](./README.zh-CN.md)**

## Core + adapter

This package is the **panel** and nothing else. It owns the React panel, the `quickControl` switch registry, the skin system, the alert surfaces, the standalone floating ⚡ trigger, and the whole host half (`src/index.ts` → `dist/index.js`). It has **no dependency on dock-base at all**, so it runs on its own, and it *always* offers the panel and the ⚡ trigger. A dock host takes the panel by claiming the `dockFlashPanel` service; only then does the core stand its own ⚡ down.

The dock-base (Workbench) integration is a separate, thin **adapter** package — `dock-flash` v3 — that depends on this one and registers the panel, the plugin card, the activity-bar item, the editor view and the command through `ctx.workbench`.

```
dsh-flash ──provides "dockFlashPanel"──▶ dock-flash ──ctx.workbench──▶ dock-base Workbench
   this package: panel, switch              the adapter: 5 registrations
   registry, skins, i18n, alerts,           + the claim/release handshake
   standalone ⚡, host routes
```

The dependency arrow points **one way**: this package never imports or names `dock-flash`. It publishes the service and stands its own ⚡ down when a host claims it; whoever claims it is a stranger it does not have to know about. That is what lets the panel work both standalone and under dock-base from one build, and why the core can be installed on a profile that has no dock-base at all.

| What you want | Install | You get |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Workbench (dock-base) integration | `dock-flash@^3`, which pulls this package in — plus `dock-base` | Sidebar/floating panel, plugin card, activity-bar ⚡, editor view, the `dock-flash:openQuickControl` command |
| Only the standalone floating ⚡ | `dsh-flash` alone | A ⚡ trigger in the configured conversation slot → floating panel |

### Upgrading from `dock-flash` v2

Nothing breaks by default. Your `^2.x` dependency range keeps you on the **old single package**, which still exists under the same name — the split added a new major (`dock-flash@^3`) rather than replacing v2. To move to the split, install `dock-flash@^3`; it depends on this package and pulls it in.

> **One profile edit is required, and it is easy to miss.** In the profile's `cordis.patch.yml` the entry that carries your panel settings reads `- id: dock-flash` / `name: dock-flash`. That `name:` is an *assertion* about the target row's current specifier, not a rename. After the split, `id: dock-flash` resolves to **this** core row, whose specifier is `dsh-flash`, so the assertion mismatches, DSH prints ``patch: name mismatch for "dock-flash" (expected "dsh-flash", got "dock-flash"), skipping`` and the whole `config:` block is **dropped** — silently reverting your panel order, your skin and your trigger position/size. Change that entry's `name: dock-flash` to `name: dsh-flash` and keep `id: dock-flash`.

> **The settings namespace itself does not change.** The profile patch **entry id** deliberately stays `dock-flash`, because that entry id *is* the settings namespace every already-published user preference lives under. The settings section, the persisted `dock-flash:…` keys and the `/plugins/dock-flash/…` host routes are all unchanged across the split — the `name:` fix above is the only edit the upgrade needs.

## Modes

| Mode | Condition | UI | Available switches |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Claimed** (Workbench) | the `dock-flash` adapter (and dock-base) installed | ⚡ in the activity bar → sidebar/floating panel; the core's standalone ⚡ is suppressed while the panel is claimed | Appearance + System |
| **Standalone** | `dsh-flash` installed alone | ⚡ trigger in the configured conversation slot → floating panel | Appearance + Layout + System |

## Features

### Built-in switches

Built-in switches are grouped into Appearance / Layout / System (compact two-column layout). The Layout group is offered in standalone mode only:

| Group | Switch | Type | Description | Standalone |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 🎨 Appearance | Theme | select | Lists what the theme service publishes, minus the dead options. While a theme publishes its **own palette** (Dream: Abyss / Aurora / …), those palettes are the list and Light / Dark / System are withheld — the palette paints over the base scheme and fixes its own colour scheme, so none of the three could do anything. With no palette published — no skin installed, **or a restyling skin such as Claude** — the list is Light / Dark / System, and Follow-system really does resolve against the OS | ✅ |
| 🎨 Appearance | Skin | select | Dynamically discovers installed skin plugins and switches between them, through DSH's **own plugin manager** — dsh-market is neither needed nor consulted. Every switch writes BOTH layers: the loader ENTRY row (what the running page acts on) and `dsh.profile.bundles` (what the next boot composes), because writing only one of them is how a skin came back after a reload, or could never be switched on again | ✅ |
| 🎨 Appearance | Turn Rail | toggle | Moves DSH's built-in turn navigator from the right gutter to the left. Hidden unless DSH's own rail is on screen and no other timeline plugin owns it | ✅ |
| 🎨 Appearance | Fullscreen | toggle | Browser Fullscreen API — enter/exit fullscreen | ✅ |
| 🎨 Appearance | Log Download | toggle | Show/hide the session log download button | ✅ |
| 📐 Layout | Close on Blur | buttongroup | Off / On — auto-close the panel when clicking outside. Also a toggle in the panel header (both modes) | ✅ |
| 📐 Layout | Trigger Position | select | Input Left / Input Right / Session Header / Header Utils — where the standalone ⚡ trigger goes — or **Conversation top-right**, a floating button inside the conversation you can drag anywhere within it | ✅ |
| 📐 Layout | Trigger Button Size | slider | 24–64 px — how big the standalone ⚡ entry point is drawn, glyph and corner radius included. The draggable **Conversation top-right** position allows the full range; the slot positions cap at **48px** so the button still fits the input row, and the row shows the size actually in force | ✅ |
| 🖱️ Right-click | *(the draggable ⚡ itself)* | menu | **Reset position** / current offset / version (click to copy a diagnostic) / **layer** and **rest opacity** presets. Not a switch in the panel: the layer and the opacity only apply to the floating button, and the menu deliberately does not repeat `trigger-size`, `trigger-position` or `close-on-blur` | ✅ |
| ⚙️ System | Language | buttongroup | 中文 / English — switches DSH global UI language | ✅ |
| ⚙️ System | Missing Companions | log | Names every companion plugin that is not **running**, splitting `installed, not running` from `not installed` — a package that is present but silent is a different problem from one that is absent. Read-only: it prints the `dsh plugin --profile <name> add …` command for the ones genuinely missing (and points at the DSH Plugins page on the reserved `desktop` profile, which the CLI refuses), plus a copy button. A ✕ hides both rows through the same visibility store the ◉ mode writes, so nothing is unregistered and ticking them again brings them back | ✅ |

> **The Layout group only renders in standalone mode.** When a host claims the panel, `close-on-blur` exists solely as the panel-header toggle, so no built-in switch carries `group: 'layout'` and the category is skipped entirely.

> **Dock layout is not configured here.** Dock edge, auto-hide, reserve space and icon scaling are dock-base's own settings — this package deliberately does not duplicate them. In the Layout group it owns only `trigger-position`, `trigger-size` and `close-on-blur`, all standalone-only.

> **Turn Rail only offers itself while DSH's own rail is what you see.** It stays hidden with no session open, in a session without turns, while DSH's own `@c

plugins.description: Sign in to ChatGPT, Claude, Copilot and other subscription model routes inside the DeepSeek Harness — the sign-in button the Harness never shipped.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-subscription-signin

[![tests](https://github.com/amosogra/dsh-subscription-signin/actions/workflows/tests.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/amosogra/dsh-subscription-signin/actions/workflows/tests.yml)

**The sign-in button the DeepSeek Harness never shipped.**

Use the AI subscriptions you already pay for — ChatGPT Plus/Pro, Claude Pro/Max,
GitHub Copilot, and more — as model routes inside the
[DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness). Adds a
**Subscriptions** settings page plus a compact extension on every provider card
in **Settings → Models**.

```text
Settings → Subscriptions → ChatGPT (Codex) → [ Sign in with ChatGPT (Codex) ]
                                    ↓
                    github.com/login/device  ·  code ABCD-1234
                                    ↓
                    ✓ Signed in — draws on your plan
```

No password is ever collected or stored by this plugin. The vendor runs the
sign-in on its own page; the Harness credential store writes the token.

## Repository layout

The **installable package is the `dsh-subscription-signin/` directory.** The
tests, license and documentation sit beside it and are not part of the package:

```text
dsh-subscription-signin/   ← the package; this is what you install
  host.js                  ← the Host half (tool + HTTP route)
  client.js                ← the Client half (settings page + provider card)
  cordis.patch.yml         ← the accounts, as configuration
  locale/en.json           ← package metadata strings
  package.json
smoketest/                 ← five dependency-free suites (run from the root)
docs/FINDINGS.md           ← what was measured vs inferred
```

---

## Why this exists

The Harness already ships everything needed to *use* a subscription as a model
route. Its LLM adapter registers OAuth flows for eight providers — the transport
works, the token exchange works, the credential store works.

What it has no surface for is **starting** one. Nothing in the GUI or CLI ever
calls the authorization seam's `begin()`. This plugin is that missing surface.

It implements **no OAuth**. It does not touch PKCE, state, device codes, or token
parsing — all of that lives in `@earendil-works/pi-ai`, shipped by DeepSeek. This
plugin asks the Harness to begin a flow, shows you the URL and code, and reports
the result.

## Supported providers

Configured out of the box, driven through the Harness's own authorization seam:

| Provider | Credential | Login style |
|---|---|---|
| ChatGPT (Codex) | `llm-pi-ai/openai-codex` | device code |
| Claude (Pro/Max) | `llm-pi-ai/anthropic` | OAuth |
| GitHub Copilot | `llm-pi-ai/github-copilot` | device code |
| xAI | `llm-pi-ai/xai` | device code |
| Meta | `llm-pi-ai/meta` | device code |
| OpenRouter | `llm-pi-ai/openrouter` | OAuth + paste fallback |
| Radius | `llm-pi-ai/radius` | browser callback |
| Kimi For Coding | `llm-pi-ai/kimi-coding` | device code |

**Honest status.** Sign-in is verified end to end for **ChatGPT (Codex)** and
**Claude (Pro/Max)**; Claude's route was observed authenticating successfully and
then being rate-limited by the account (HTTP 429 with Anthropic's own
`request_id` — a quota answer, not a credential failure). Copilot's flow is
verified and completes. xAI, Meta, OpenRouter, Radius and Kimi hold credentials
that have been written successfully, but **no request has been served on those
routes in the session where this was verified**, so treat them as untested rather
than broken. `docs/FINDINGS.md` records what is measured versus inferred.

## Install

**Requirements.** DeepSeek Harness `0.2.0-rc.2` or later. Developed and verified
against `0.2.0-rc.2`, the release this plugin's two seams were checked on
(`ctx.authorization` from `@deepseek-ai/dsh-authorization`, and the client
`slots` service). Every Harness service it consumes is reached with a defensive
`ctx.get(...)` plus an undefined check, so a missing one degrades to a reported
message instead of a crash — but a Harness that has moved a seam will still need
a matching plugin release.

The plugin is installed into a Harness **profile** as a bundle. Point the plugin
manager at this directory:

```text
install_bundle: link:/absolute/path/to/dsh-subscription-signin
```

Or, if you publish/consume it as a package, install by name and add it to your
profile's bundle list:

```jsonc
// $DSH_PROFILE_DIR/package.json
"dsh": { "profile": { "bundles": ["@deepseek-ai/dsh-base", "@deepseek-ai/dsh-web-app", "dsh-subscription-signin"] } }
```

Then **restart DSH once.** This matters and is explained under
[Troubleshooting](#troubleshooting) — the client half is composed into the
browser's boot graph at startup, so a freshly installed bundle has no page until
the process restarts.

## Use

From the GUI: **Settings → Subscriptions**, pick an account, press *Sign in*.

For an agent, or a headless harness, the same implementation is exposed as a tool
with actions `status`, `start`, `poll`, `cancel`, `signout`, `submitCode` and
`diagnostics`. Read `status` first; `start` returns the URL and, for device
grants, the code you enter on the vendor's page.

## Safety

This section is the reason to trust the plugin, so it is specific rather than
reassuring.

**It never sees a secret.** No password, token, API key or refresh token is read,
written, logged, or forwarded. The token is produced and stored by the Harness
credential seam (`ctx.authorization` / `ctx.credentials`), not by this code.
Audit it yourself — it is two files:

- **`host.js`** — zero imports. No filesystem access, no network requests, no
  child processes. It asks the credential store *whether* a record exists, and
  can delete one on explicit `signout` with `confirm: true`; it never reads a
  token value. The one `process.env` write is the documented per-account `env`
  field (used so a provider that selects its endpoint from the environment can be
  configured per account), and it is restored when the attempt settles.
- **`client.js`** — one dependency, `react`, supplied by the page. Its only
  `fetch` calls go to the plugin's own `/plugins/subscription-signin` route on
  your local Harness. Nothing is rendered from a credential.

**The one network-bearing route is trust-gated.** The panel reaches the Host half
over an HTTP route that inherits the Harness's own checks
(`connection.requestRejection`: Host/Origin validation and browser
authentication). On top of that, every mutating call must be a JSON `POST`, which
forces a CORS preflight and blocks form-based CSRF; bodies are capped at 64 KiB;
responses are `no-store` + `nosniff`.

**Not sanctioned by the vendors — read this.** For ChatGPT-plan usage, the
Harness targets the ChatGPT/Codex backend
(`chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex`), which OpenAI's developer documentation tells
third-party apps not to target for plan usage. **This plugin surfaces behaviour
the Harness already ships; it does not introduce it and cannot change it.** The
sanctioned path for third-party apps is *Sign in with ChatGPT*, which the Harness
does not implement. Using a subscription outside a vendor's intended client may
conflict with that vendor's terms, and vendors may rate-limit or block such
traffic. You are choosing to do that with your own account. Do not use this to
resell access, and do not use it to reach credentials that are not yours.

**No credentials are in this repository.** If you ever find one here, that is a
bug — please open an issue. The repository was scanned for tokens, private keys,
home paths and email addresses before its first commit. `docs/FINDINGS.md` does
cite exact package versions and source symbols from the Harness, which is
deliberate: a claim about a specific build is only useful if it names the build.

**Found a vulnerability?** Report it privately via
[SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) rather than a public issue. That file also lists what
is and is not in scope — worth reading first, because the unofficial-backend
caveat above is a documented trade-off rather than a defect, and the two are easy
to confuse.

## Configuration

Accounts are configured, not hardcoded. They live in this package's own
[`cordis.patch.yml`](dsh-subscripti

plugins.description: A transparent always-on-top desktop pet for DSH on Linux (X11 / XWayland)
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-pet-desktop-linux

[**English**](README.md) | [中文](README.zh.md)

A desktop pet for DSH (DeepSeek Harness) on Linux: a small transparent,
always-on-top GTK3 window that floats over your desktop and animates according to
what your DSH sessions are doing — idle, working, waiting for an answer, failed,
or finished and awaiting review. It is not click-through: the window keeps its
input region, so clicks on the pet land on the pet.

**Platform: Linux with X11 or XWayland only.** Windows, macOS and native Wayland
(no XWayland) are not supported. See [Requirements](#requirements).

![The pet floating transparently over the desktop](assets/screenshots/desktop-pet-linux-1.png)

The window has no background and no border — the wallpaper shows through, and the
pet stays on top of ordinary windows. The sprite follows your DSH sessions:

![Idle, working, waiting, failed and review poses](assets/screenshots/desktop-pet-linux-2.png)

> **Canonical copy:** this plugin is only published as
> `dsh-pet-desktop-linux` (no scope) under the `Wlaeg` account. Any other
> package with this name is not ours.

---

## This is not a meta-package

This plugin ships **its own working program**; it is not a bundle that only
re-exports somebody else's dependency list:

| Part | File | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| Desktop program | `desktop/pet.py` | The pet window itself: GTK3 transparent window, spritesheet animation, right-click menu, work-status dialog |
| Host half | `lib/index.js` | Probes system dependencies, spawns/stops the Python program, exposes the HTTP routes, reads and writes the config file |
| Browser half | `client.js` | The **Desktop Pet** panel in DSH Settings, with the packaged `locale/{en,zh}.json` manifest strings |

The single dependency, `@michengai/dsh-codex-pet`, is used **only to read the pet
sprite sheets**. This plugin deliberately does not copy that artwork into its own
repository: store rules require a bundle's dependencies to resolve to the original
author's published package, so this plugin depends on the upstream npm package
and resolves the artwork path at runtime
(`require.resolve('@michengai/dsh-codex-pet/package.json')`). See
[Artwork and licensing](#artwork-and-licensing).

The upstream plugin draws a pet **inside the DSH web page**. This plugin draws a
**separate always-on-top desktop window** that works while the page is in the
background, minimized, or closed. They are different things, not duplicates.

---

## Requirements

| Item | Requirement |
|---|---|
| Platform | **Linux with X11 or XWayland.** Verified on Manjaro GNOME (Wayland session, pet runs through XWayland) |
| DSH | Any DSH build with the Cordis plugin system that provides `webServer` and the `settings.section` slot |
| Node | **>= 22** (DSH's own requirement) |
| Desktop session | A GTK3-capable session. Under GNOME/Wayland the pet is an XWayland client — a **pure Wayland session with XWayland disabled will not work** |
| npm dependencies | `@michengai/dsh-codex-pet` (artwork lookup only) |

### System packages

The Settings panel probes five of these — Python 3, PyGObject, GTK3, GdkPixbuf
and `xdotool` — and shows the matching install hint for your distribution when
one is missing. The other two rows (the WebP loader and `zstd`) are not probed;
check them yourself with the commands below if the pet starts but looks wrong.

| Component | Arch / Manjaro | Debian / Ubuntu | Fedora |
|---|---|---|---|
| Python 3 | `python` | `python3` | `python3` |
| Python 3 + PyGObject (`import gi`) | `python-gobject` | `python3-gi` | `python3-gobject` |
| GTK3 typelib | `gtk3` | `gir1.2-gtk-3.0` | `gtk3` |
| GdkPixbuf typelib | `gdk-pixbuf2` | `gir1.2-gdkpixbuf-2.0` | `gdk-pixbuf2` |
| WebP loader for GdkPixbuf | *(built into `gdk-pixbuf2`)* | `webp-pixbuf-loader` | `webp-pixbuf-loader` |
| `zstd` CLI *(only if Python < 3.14)* | `zstd` | `zstd` | `zstd` |
| xdotool | `xdotool` | `xdotool` | `xdotool` |

```sh
# Arch / Manjaro
sudo pacman -S python python-gobject gtk3 gdk-pixbuf2 zstd xdotool

# Debian / Ubuntu
sudo apt install python3 python3-gi gir1.2-gtk-3.0 gir1.2-gdkpixbuf-2.0 webp-pixbuf-loader zstd xdotool

# Fedora
sudo dnf install python3 python3-gobject gtk3 gdk-pixbuf2 webp-pixbuf-loader zstd xdotool
```

The session event files are zstd-compressed. Python 3.14 and newer decode them
with the standard library (`compression.zstd`); on older interpreters the plugin
falls back to the `zstd` command-line tool, so install `zstd` if your `python3`
is older than 3.14. Without either, the pet still runs but never leaves `idle`.

The sprite sheets are WebP files, so GdkPixbuf must be able to decode WebP.
Depending on your distribution's GdkPixbuf version this may need the separate
`webp-pixbuf-loader` package (Debian/Ubuntu, Fedora). You can check yours with
the command below; if it prints `False`, install the loader package:

```sh
python3 -c "import gi; gi.require_version('GdkPixbuf','2.0'); \
from gi.repository import GdkPixbuf; \
print('webp' in [f.get_name() for f in GdkPixbuf.Pixbuf.get_formats()])"
```

The plugin's dependency probe checks GTK3, GdkPixbuf and `xdotool` by name but
does not decode a WebP sprite itself; if the loader is missing, the pet window
appears and the sprite fails to load, which shows up in the log tail.

`xdotool` is used for the two EWMH window hints GTK3 cannot set by itself:
`_NET_WM_STATE_ABOVE` (keep above) and `_NET_WM_STATE_STICKY` (show on every
workspace). Without it the pet still appears, but it will not stay on top of
other windows or follow you across workspaces.

Decoding goes through `GdkPixbuf.PixbufLoader` and frames are drawn as
`Gtk.Image` pixbufs, so **Pillow is not needed**, and because no drawing goes
through a `cairo.Context`, **pycairo is not needed either**.

---

## Installation

This is a DSH Cordis plugin **bundle**. Install it through DSH's plugin manager
(`plugin_manager`, action `install_bundle`), pointing `target` at either:

- the **Git repository** — `https://github.com/Wlaeg/dsh-pet-desktop-linux`
- or a **local checkout** — the absolute path to this directory

Equivalently, from a DSH shell:

```sh
# once published to npm
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-pet-desktop-linux

# straight from the repository
dsh plugin --profile web add github:Wlaeg/dsh-pet-desktop-linux

# from a local checkout
dsh plugin --profile web add /absolute/path/to/dsh-pet-desktop-linux
```

The bundle declares its own patch in `package.json`:

```json
{
  "dsh": {
    "bundle": { "patch": "./cordis.patch.yml" },
    "client": {
      "platform": "web",
      "immediately": true,
      "inject": ["@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-locale", "@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-renderer"]
    }
  },
  "icon": "./assets/icon.png"
}
```

(`dsh.client.inject` is a client-module **load-order** declaration: DSH loads the
listed packages' browser bundles before this one. It is not Cordis service
injection. The browser half declares the services it actually needs itself:
`return { inject: ['slots', 'locale'], apply }`.)

and that patch is a single `insert` that mounts the host half:

```yaml
- insert:
    - id: dsh-pet-desktop-linux
      name: 'dsh-pet-desktop-linux'
      config: {}
```

The browser half is declared by `dsh.client` and bound to the row whose `name` is
the bare package name — subpath rows do not carry a browser half.

After installing, reload the DSH Web UI page so the browser half registers its
Settings panel. Nothing else is required: **DSH starts the pet window by itself**
as soon as it boots (`autostart` defaults to `true` — see “Configuration”). The
pet process stops when you stop it or uninstall the bundle.

> Replacing an already-installed copy (for example after editing the source)
> needs a restart of the DSH host process — the running process keeps the JS
> module generation it loaded at startup. A page reload is not enough.

---

## Features

**Window**

- Borderless, transparent GTK3 window — only the pet is visible, the window
  background is fully transparent
- Always on top (`_NET_WM_STATE_ABOVE`), so it stays above normal windows
- Sticky across workspaces (`_NET_WM_STATE_STICKY`, via `xdotool`) — no API for
  this exists in GT

plugins.description: OpenCode Zen free models for DeepSeek Harness, with live catalog discovery and no dependencies.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-zen-adapter

把 [OpenCode Zen](https://opencode.ai/zen) 的**免费模型**接入 DeepSeek Harness，
注册为原生 provider `zen-free`。

无需注册、无需 API key、无需额外进程。

[English](README.en.md) | 简体中文

---

## 特性

- **零配置** — 装上、重启、就能在模型选择器里选到免费模型
- **零依赖** — `dependencies` 为空，运行时复用 DSH 自带的 pi-ai，因此可以和其他
  provider 插件共存（详见[为什么零依赖很重要](#为什么零依赖很重要)）
- **动态模型目录** — 从上游实时发现，不是写死的清单，上游换模型不用等插件更新
- **可用性检测** — 区分「目录里在售」和「这台机器真的能调通」，避免选到用不了的模型
- **可视化面板** — 在插件详情页一键获取模型、检测可用性，并查看上下文大小

## 安装

```powershell
dsh plugin --profile <你的 profile> add github:seonzzy/dsh-zen-adapter
# 或从本地目录安装：
dsh plugin --profile <你的 profile> add <本目录绝对路径>
```

装完**重启 DSH**，然后在模型选择器里选择 **OpenCode Zen (free lane)** 分组下的模型。

### 前提条件

| 条件 | 说明 |
| --- | --- |
| DSH 版本 | 需要带 `llm.registerAdapter` 与 `webServer` 的版本 |
| Node | ≥ 20（DSH 自带，无需另装）|
| 网络 | 能访问 `opencode.ai` 与 `models.dev` |

不需要安装 pi-ai、不需要 API key、不需要 npm/pnpm 下载任何东西。

## 使用

### 模型选择器

安装后在对话输入框的模型选择器里会出现 **OpenCode Zen (free lane)** 分组，
选择其中一个模型即可开始对话。

目录会**动态获取**：启动时后台拉取，之后每 30 分钟自动刷新一次。

### 插件面板

在「设置 → 插件 → dsh-zen-adapter」页面上有一个面板：

| 按钮 | 作用 |
| --- | --- |
| **获取模型** | 从上游重新拉取模型目录 |
| **检测可用性** | 逐个真实请求，测出哪些模型当前可用 |

下面的表格展示：模型名、上下文大小、输出上限、可用状态、判定依据。

> **「目录里有」不等于「能用」。** 免费模型的实际可用性受上游端点状态、
> 地区限制、以及**按 IP 计的配额**影响，随时会变。建议在新环境里点一次
> 「检测可用性」。

## 模型是怎么来的

插件同时读取两个上游数据源，取交集：

| 源 | 提供 | 不提供 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `opencode.ai/zen/v1/models` | 当前**在售**的模型 id | 价格、上下文 |
| `models.dev/api.json` | `cost`、`limit.context`、`limit.output` | 是否在售 |

第二个源是必需的——Zen 的 `/v1/models` 只返回 `{ id, object, created, owned_by }`，
**无法从它判断某模型是否免费**。

**免费判定**以 models.dev 的 `cost` 为准（`input` 与 `output` 均为 0）。
已弃用或收费的模型即使 id 带 `-free` 也不会放行——上游会把下架模型在目录里
继续挂一段时间。只有 metadata 缺失时（通常是刚发布的新模型）才退回看 `-free` 后缀。

上下文大小与输出上限同样来自 models.dev，所以界面上显示的是真实数值，
不是某个固定常数。

## 为什么零依赖很重要

本插件**不声明任何 `dependencies`**，`@deepseek-ai/*` 与 `@earendil-works/pi-ai`
全部声明为 `peerDependencies` 且标记 `optional`。

原因：DSH 宿主自带一份 pi-ai，插件运行时沿宿主的模块树解析，全局始终只有一份。

如果插件自带一份 pi-ai，机器上就会出现**两个 pi-ai 世代**。这不只是冗余——
某些插件（例如 `dsh-workbuddy-xdpool`）会校验宿主与插件用的是不是同一世代，
不一致时整个 provider 每次调用都会失败。

因此本插件可以和其他 provider 插件**同时安装**。

## 上游限制

OpenCode 的免费通道**按 IP 计配额**，部分模型还有**地区限制**。

可能遇到的情况：

| 现象 | 原因 | 怎么办 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `429` | 配额用尽或请求过密 | 等一会儿再试，或换网络节点 |
| `403 RegionError` | 该模型不对你所在地区开放 | 无法绕过，换其他模型 |
| `5xx` / `400` | 上游端点暂时故障 | 换其他模型，稍后再试 |
| 模型不在选择器里 | 尚未被判定为免费 | 点「获取模型」刷新目录 |

这些都属于**上游侧**行为，插件无法修复。用「检测可用性」可以看到每个模型的
当前状态。

## 配置

本插件没有需要配置的选项。如需调整可选行为，可修改 `lib/index.js` 顶部的常量：

| 常量 | 默认 | 说明 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `PROVIDER_ID` | `zen-free` | 在 DSH 中显示的 provider id |
| `SEED_MODELS` | 3 个模型 | 目录拉取完成前的占位列表 |
| 目录刷新间隔 | 30 分钟 | 见 `lib/index.js` 中的 `refreshTimer` |

## 卸载

```powershell
dsh plugin --profile <你的 profile> remove dsh-zen-adapter
```

然后重启 DSH。

## 许可

MIT

plugins.description: Discord and Feishu/Lark channels for DeepSeek Harness: verified identities, shared sessions, native Ask User and progress delivery.
plugins.readme_text:
# Channel Core for DeepSeek Harness

[简体中文](README.zh-CN.md) · [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) · [Security](SECURITY.md)

**One plugin for Discord and Feishu/Lark channels**, with shared session routing, verified owner identity, reliable message delivery, and progress/status integration.

## Features

- Discord and Feishu adapters live in the same package with independent credentials and connection lifecycles.
- Map verified direct messages from the same owner to a shared **native DSH session** when explicitly configured.
- Durable inbound receipts, serialized session admission, and native steer/queue/interrupt handling avoid replaying messages.
- Native Ask User interactions and progress/status integration preserve conversational continuity.
- Owner verification guards personal-memory access and cross-channel session transitions.

## Proactive outbound messaging

Channel Core supports **agent-initiated outbound messages** without a preceding inbound message. The `channel_send` tool can send a text message from the current native DSH session to its **already bound and currently authorized** Feishu or Discord conversation. The host/plugin API `ctx.channelCore.sendToBoundSession({ sessionId, text, idempotencyKey, bindingId?, source? })` allows trusted schedulers and other integrations to send the same way; `outboundTargets(sessionId)` lists eligible binding IDs without exposing destination identifiers.

- **Scope:** A session can send only to its own eligible bindings. Multiple bindings require an explicit `bindingId`; arbitrary recipient IDs and cross-session delivery are not accepted. Group allowlists and current DM/owner permission are checked again on send.
- **Delivery:** Uses the existing durable outbox and platform send adapters, with state `pending`, `sent`, `failed`, or `uncertain`. Reusing a stable idempotency key does not send the same message twice. A potentially delivered but unacknowledged message is **not** blindly retried.
- **Automation:** Jobs can call `channel_send` after creating a report (e.g. a scheduled financial report), or trusted plugins can call `sendToBoundSession` directly. This does **not** automatically broadcast every scheduled result, and it does not grant an agent permission to send to arbitrary accounts.
- **Testing:** `npm test` runs dependency-free public regressions. `npm run test:host` runs the broader integration suite inside a configured DSH developer environment with host peer dependencies. Live Feishu/Discord delivery has been separately exercised locally; CI cannot verify third-party credentials.

## Install

Requires a compatible DSH host with the peer services in [package.json](package.json), and credentials for each channel you choose to enable.

```sh
dsh plugin --profile desktop add github:Kerberos255/dsh-channel-core
```

Use your DSH profile name. Pin an installation to a Git commit if reproducibility is required. Restart DSH after installing or updating code.

## Quick start

1. Open **Settings → Plugins → Channels & Sessions**.
2. Configure the **Discord** and/or **Feishu** tab, platform credentials, and allowed users/channels. A valid connection alone does not authorize message delivery.
3. Review the owner-identification mode in each channel. Automatic first-DM owner claim occurs only after the incoming message passes channel allow rules; manual owner selection is available.
4. Optional: link owner accounts when you want **the same live DSH session** across channels. Sharing verified long-term memory does not require sharing a session.
5. Send a test DM and check the bound workspace, session, and progress output.

## Security and operational boundaries

A channel owner is verified per bot account; group conversations and unverified users must not inherit personal-memory authority. Session mapping decisions are audited and cannot silently reuse sessions from another workspace. The native Host manages agent execution, cancellations, jobs, and saved histories. The plugin keeps independent delivery and receipt state, not a second model engine.

Settings and channel files are local to DSH; do not upload credentials, binding databases, or historical messages. Source template: [config.example.json](config.example.json).

## Testing and related projects

Run `npm test` for portable regressions. **A green CI run does not prove live Discord, Feishu, or network authentication.** Verify actual bot delivery and UI interactions in your own host.

Related: [Status Cards](https://github.com/Kerberos255/dsh-status-cards) · [Dream & Memory](https://github.com/Kerberos255/dsh-memory-dreaming) · [Lossless Context](https://github.com/Kerberos255/dsh-lossless-context).

MIT licensed. See [LICENSE](LICENSE). Historical release notes: [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md).

## Streaming and progress

Discord shows thought, draft and tool activity in a single rolling progress message. When native assistant messages include separate committed interim text and a final reply, the completed message presents the interim text as a native Markdown blockquote and keeps the formal answer outside it. The runtime footer remains optional; long replies are split to fit Discord message limits. Ask User preserves committed pre-question text as an independent quoted draft card before the interactive prompt, so later replies do not re-send the same text. Live draft previews use only the 📝 icon without synthetic section names.

Feishu supports CardKit component-level streaming with an IM-card compatibility fallback, agent role labels, and independently configurable runtime footer fields. Draft and thinking are separate switches: turning off thinking keeps public draft text visible. Completed turns may retain a collapsed **📝 过程记录** card containing enabled non-duplicate draft/thinking entries. Ask User freezes the preceding progress/context card and sends a separate interactive question card, without erasing the visible lead-in. The per-channel refresh intervals and progress budgets are configurable; real platform permissions and latency still need validation in your own environment.

## Ask User completion and optional diagnostics

Discord and Feishu now update the original Ask User message to a read-only completion receipt containing the submitted question and selected/custom answer, with controls removed. Historical pre-question text is non-interactive; Feishu stage records use a collapsed panel. The channels optionally emit privacy-restricted event and failure metadata through the dsh-plugin-diagnostics service when installed. The diagnostics plugin is not required for normal channel operation.

## Channel slash commands and outbound delivery

Discord registers flat `/new`, `/stop`, `/status`, `/session`, `/answer`, `/prompt`, `/model` and `/think` application commands. Replacement commands register before the deprecated `/dsh` group is removed. Feishu accepts text `/new`, `/stop`, `/status`, `/session`, `/answer`, `/model` and `/think`. Feishu `/model provider` selects only when that provider has exactly one available model; otherwise it lists candidates. `/model` and `/think` show usage before the candidate list. Model changes take effect on the next turn.

Verified sessions may send messages to **existing authorized channel bindings** via the `channel_send` tool or the trusted `sendToBoundSession` integration. Outbound messages use a durable delivery queue and idempotency keys; arbitrary recipients are not accepted. See the source tests for owner and delivery security coverage.

CI runs host-independent unit tests with `npm test`. The complete channel adapter integration suite (`npm run test:integration`) requires a DSH host with the declared peer services and must be run in that environment before release.

plugins.description: Multi-directory workspaces for DeepSeek Harness.
plugins.readme_text:
dsh-plugin-addir

让 DeepSeek Harness 支持多根目录工作区与上下文动态注入
灵感来自 OpenAI Codex --add-dir 与现代 AI IDE 多根目录工作区设计

简体中文 | English

--- ## 💡 为什么需要 addir？ 在默认情况下，[DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) 的工作区通常只绑定一个工作目录（Primary Root）。当面临以下复杂开发场景时常常受限： - **跨仓库 / 跨模块协作**：前后端工程分离（如 `frontend/` 与 `backend/`），智能体需要同时理解接口定义与业务实现； - **共享代码与公共库**：项目依赖独立的公共组件库（如 `shared-ui/`、`core-lib/`），需要跨目录检索却不想反复复制代码； - **只读规格与文档参照**：引入只读的设计规范、API 契约或第三方代码，需要智能体参考但**绝不允许误改**。 `dsh-plugin-addir` 彻底打破单一工作区限制！它支持在当前工作区下**关联任意多个外部目录**，配合直观的图形化管理界面、自动上下文注入与细粒度只读保护，让智能体自如跨目录协同工作。 --- ## ✨ 核心特性 - 📁 **多根目录关联（Multi-Root Workspaces）** 支持为任意工作区挂载多个额外文件夹，为每个目录配置易记的别名（Alias）、描述信息及只读（Read-Only）标记。 - 🧠 **上下文动态注入（Context Injection）** 每轮对话自动将当前生效的目录树注入给大模型上下文。智能体可直接理解 `[别名]/path` 或 `别名:path` 路径简写。 - 🛡️ **细粒度只读防护（Read-Only Protection）** 勾选 `只读` 的目录将被文件工具守卫拦截 `write` / `edit` 操作，彻底避免智能体误改公共依赖或文档。 - 🖥️ **无缝原生 UI（Native GUI Integration）** 深度集成 DSH 工作区列表菜单（`⋯` → 编辑）。弹窗支持调用系统原生目录选择器，体验丝滑自然。 - 💾 **跨会话持久化（Auto Persistence）** 关联关系按工作区根路径隔离并持久化至本地存储（`$DSH_HOME/storages/addir.json`），应用重启后自动恢复。 - 🤖 **智能体自主管理（Agent Tools）** 内置 `addir_list`、`addir_add`、`addir_remove` 工具，允许智能体在对话中动态扩展视野；也可一键关闭权限，由用户完全掌控。 --- ## 🖥️ 界面展示 ### 1. 工作区菜单入口 在工作区列表中点击目标项目的「`⋯`」按钮，选择「**编辑**」： ![工作区菜单](assets/workspace-menu.png) ### 2. 多目录图形化管理弹窗 支持修改工作区名称、使用**系统原生目录选择器**添加文件夹、配置个性化别名，并可单独勾选「只读」权限： ![编辑项目弹窗](assets/workspace-editor.png) --- ## 注入到模型的上下文示例 启用 `enableContextInjection` 后，插件会在每轮对话自动向大模型注入当前工作区的生效目录表： ```markdown # Active Workspace Directories - [primary] `/Users/dev/repo/frontend` (Primary root) - [backend] `/Users/dev/repo/backend` - 核心 API 服务 - [specs] `/Users/dev/repo/api-specs` [Read-Only] - OpenAPI 契约定义 ``` 智能体能够据此识别每个目录的作用，并使用 `[backend]/src/app.ts` 或直接使用绝对路径进行高效分析。 --- ## 🚀 快速上手 1. **安装插件**（参考下方[安装指南](#-安装指南)）； 2. **关联目录**：在工作区列表点击「`⋯`」→「编辑」，点击「**添加文件夹**」选择本地目录，设置别名（如 `backend`）并保存； 3. **开始对话**：直接对智能体说： > *"请阅读 [backend] 目录下的路由定义，并在当前前端项目中生成对应的 API 请求函数。"* --- ## 📦 安装指南 ### 1. 通过 DSH 插件市场 / 设置面板安装 打开 DeepSeek Harness 桌面端或 Web 端，进入 **设置 → 插件管理**，搜索 `dsh-plugin-addir`，点击安装即可。 ### 2. 通过命令行安装（推荐） ```sh # Web Profile（推荐在 Web 版使用） dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-plugin-addir # 桌面端 Desktop Profile # 注意：桌面端首次使用请先启动一次应用以初始化 profile，完全退出应用后再执行安装命令，随后重新打开应用 dsh plugin --profile desktop add dsh-plugin-addir # Headless / 自定义 Profile dsh plugin --profile headless add dsh-plugin-addir ``` > [!NOTE] > 本插件自带 **bundle patch**（`cordis.patch.yml`），安装时会自动向 profile 注册 `id: addir`，**无需手动修改配置文件**。 ### 3. 从源码构建安装（开发者模式） ```sh # 克隆仓库 git clone https://github.com/keatsyh/dsh-plugin-addir.git cd dsh-plugin-addir # 安装依赖并构建（prepare 会自动编译 lib/ 产物） pnpm install # 软链接安装到目标 profile dsh plugin --profile web add "link:$PWD" ``` --- ## ⚙️ 配置说明 所有配置项均有合理的默认值。您可以在 DSH 的**插件设置页**中直观调整，或在 profile 对应的 `cordis.patch.yml` 中进行配置覆盖： | 配置项 | 类型 | 默认值 | 说明 | |---|---|---|---| | `enableTools` | `boolean` | `true` | 是否向智能体暴露 `addir_*` 工具（允许模型自己增删目录） | | `enableContextInjection` | `boolean` | `true` | 是否在每轮对话开始前向系统提示词注入工作区目录表 | | `enforceReadOnly` | `boolean` | `true` | 是否在底层工具拦截对标记为只读目录的文件写入与编辑 | | `defaultDirectories` | `Array` | `[]` | 启动时预先关联的静态目录列表（包含 `path`, `alias`, `description`, `readOnly`） | ### YAML 配置示例 ```yaml - id: addir config: enableTools: false # 仅允许在 UI 界面中手动管理，禁止智能体自行增删 enableContextInjection: true # 保持提示词注入 enforceReadOnly: true # 开启只读保护 defaultDirectories: - path: /data/docs/specs alias: specs description: API 规范文档 readOnly: true ``` > [!TIP] > 界面中所做的新增、编辑和删除操作，会实时持久化在 `$DSH_HOME/storages/addir.json` 中，按规范化工作区根路径索引，无需担心重启丢失。 --- ## 🛠️ 智能体工具（Agent Tools） 当 `enableTools` 开启时，智能体可自主使用以下工具： | 工具名称 | 参数 | 说明 | |---|---|---| | `addir_list` | — | 查看当前工作区已关联的所有目录（包括主根目录、别名、描述与只读标记） | | `addir_add` | `path` (必填)
`alias` (可选)
`description` (可选)
`readOnly` (可选) | 动态关联一个额外目录。支持传入绝对路径或相对工作区主目录的路径 | | `addir_remove` | `pathOrAlias` (必填) | 解除关联指定目录（支持按绝对路径或别名查找，主根目录不可移除） | 如不希望智能体拥有自主挂载权限，只需将配置中的 `enableTools` 设为 `false`。 --- ## 🧩 开发者 API 其他插件或扩展可以通过 Cordis 服务上下文直接调用 `ctx.addir`： ```ts import type { Context } from '@deepseek-ai/cordis' export function apply(ctx: Context) { // 获取当前会话下关联的目录列表 const dirs = ctx.addir.list(sessionId) // 动态关联额外目录 ctx.addir.add({ path: '/path/to/shared-lib', alias: 'shared', description: 'Shared utilities', readOnly: true, }, sessionId) // 解析带别名的路径为真实绝对路径（例如 '[shared]/utils.ts' -> '/path/to/shared-lib/utils.ts'） const resolved = ctx.addir.resolvePath('[shared]/utils.ts', sessionId) // 检查某个路径是否归属于当前工作区或其关联目录 const isIncluded = ctx.addir.isUnderWorkspace('/path/to/file.ts', sessionId) // 检查某个路径是否处于只读保护范围内 const isReadOnly = ctx.addir.isReadOnly('/path/to/file.ts', sessionId) } ``` --- ## ❓ 常见问题 (FAQ)
Q: 桌面端（Desktop）安装后没有出现「编辑」菜单？ 桌面端应用在首次安装插件时，需要完全退出应用进程（macOS 请使用 `Cmd + Q`，Windows 请从托盘或任务管理器完全退出），再次启动应用使客户端扩展脚本加载生效。
Q: 标记为只读的目录，智能体还可以阅读或搜索代码吗？ 可以。只读保护仅拦截 `write`、`edit` 等修改文件的工具调用，代码阅读（`read`）、检索（`grep` / `glob`）等完全正常运作。
Q: 可以在多个不同的工作区中使用相同的别名吗？ 可以。目录关联数据是严格按照各工作区的根目录路径隔离存储的，不同工作区之间的别名互不影响。
Q: 如何防止智能体自作主张关联新目录？ 在 DSH 插件设置中将 **`enableTools`** 开关关闭（或在配置文件中设为 `false`），智能体将不再拥有 `addir_*` 工具，但您依然可以在 GUI 弹窗中手动管理目录。
--- ## 💻 本地开发 ```sh # 安装依赖 pnpm install # 运行单元测试与集成测试 pnpm test # 类型检查 pnpm run typecheck # 构建打包（含 client bundle 语法检查与 d.ts 生成） pnpm run build ``` > **架构提示**：客户端代码采用经典脚本与 DSH 共享模块加载器注册（`window.__ModuleLoader__.load`），使用宿主提供的 React 运行时。工作区菜单入口通过 DOM 适配器挂载（`src/client/workspace-menu.ts`）。 --- ## 📄 License 本项目基于 [MIT 许可证](LICENSE) 开源。

plugins.description: DeepSeek Harness 插件：侧边栏实时余额 + 每轮对话花费（人民币，含 token 明细）
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-deepseek-usage

一个 DeepSeek Harness (dsh) 插件，做两件事：

1. **侧边栏余额**：在左下角「设置」旁边实时显示 DeepSeek 账户余额（默认每 60 秒刷新；点击可展开充值余额 / 赠送余额并手动刷新；侧栏收窄成图标栏时显示为彩色状态点）。
2. **每轮对话花费**：在每一轮对话底部的信息栏里额外显示**这一轮花了多少钱**，点击可展开三列明细（项目 / tokens / 单价）。

> 只适用于**官方 DeepSeek（`deepseek-official`）** 且在**带 Web 界面的 profile**（`desktop` 或 `web`）里使用。用其他 provider 时余额读不到、也不该按 DeepSeek 价目计价。

## 关于安装入口（曾踩过的坑）

部分第三方桌面客户端内置的「插件市场」有一条硬性边界：**只接受 `包名@精确版本` 这种 npm 目标**，`github:` 源、`file:` 路径、裸包名一律拒绝。遇到这种客户端时，市场的报错大致是：

> 这个桌面客户端只能安装已发布到 npm 的插件，而该插件仅提供 GitHub 源，因此装不了——这是客户端的安装边界，不是插件或市场的问题。可以改用普通 dsh web 安装，或请插件作者发布 npm 包。

**本插件现已发布到 npm**（`@blackthunder2191026/dsh-deepseek-usage`），因此这条边界不再是问题：用「方式一」或「方式二」都能装。如果市场仍报上面的错，说明你用的市场缓存了旧目录，或你点的是插件的 GitHub 条目而不是 npm 条目。

## 环境要求

| 项目 | 要求 |
|---|---|
| 操作系统 | Windows / macOS / Linux 均可（本插件不含平台相关代码，未使用任何平台专有 API） |
| dsh | 带 Web 界面的 profile（官方桌面版或 `dsh web`）；headless / SDK profile 没有 webserver，插件不会生效 |
| Node.js | ≥ 22.19（宿主读取余额用 `fetch` 与 `AbortSignal.timeout`） |
| DeepSeek 凭据 | 官方 provider 的 API Key，存在 `~/.dsh/.credentials.yaml` 的 `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`，或同名环境变量 |
| 依赖 | **零运行时依赖**：host 半不 import 任何包，client 半只向 dsh 的模块表要 `react` |

## 安装

包名是 **`@blackthunder2191026/dsh-deepseek-usage`**（带 scope，因为 npm 上 `dsh-deepseek-usage` 已被无关项目占用）。

### 方式一：命令行从 npm 安装（推荐）

```sh
npx @deepseek-ai/dsh plugin --profile desktop add @blackthunder2191026/dsh-deepseek-usage
```

**装完重启 dsh。**

### 方式二：从图形插件市场安装

市场只会把 `包名@精确版本` 交给客户端，所以本插件**发布到 npm 之后**可以从市场一键安装——在市场的搜索框里找 `dsh-deepseek-usage`，或直接粘贴上面的完整包名。

> 如果你在市场里看到过「只能安装已发布到 npm 的插件，而该插件仅提供 GitHub 源」这样的提示，说明你用的是**本插件还没有 npm 版本时**的市场状态，或者你点的是插件的 GitHub 条目。请改用方式一，或先确认版本。

### 方式三：从 GitHub 源码安装（无需 npm）

```sh
npx @deepseek-ai/dsh plugin --profile desktop add github:BlackThunder2191026/dsh-deepseek-usage
```

pnpm 默认会拦截 Git 依赖的构建脚本。本插件**没有任何编译步骤**，但仍带一个 `prepare` 安装钩子（`tools/prepare.mjs`）用于完整性检查；若安装时被拦下，按提示在该 profile 的 `pnpm-workspace.yaml` 里加上：

```yaml
allowBuilds:
  '@blackthunder2191026/dsh-deepseek-usage': true
```

> ⚠️ `allowBuilds` 表示**允许该包的安装脚本在你的机器上执行**。本插件的钩子只做一件事：检查四个关键文件存在且非空，缺任何一个就拒绝安装——它不编译、不下载、不访问网络。**授权前请先读一遍 `tools/prepare.mjs`。** 想更稳妥可锁定 commit：`github:BlackThunder2191026/dsh-deepseek-usage#<sha>`。

### 方式四：从 Releases 下载 tarball（无需 Git、无需 npm、无需授权脚本）

每个版本都会在 [Releases](https://github.com/BlackThunder2191026/dsh-deepseek-usage/releases) 附上 `blackthunder2191026-dsh-deepseek-usage-<版本>.tgz`：

```sh
# 下载后在下载目录执行
npx @deepseek-ai/dsh plugin --profile desktop add ./blackthunder2191026-dsh-deepseek-usage-1.0.0.tgz
```

### ⚠️ 从旧版本（不带 scope 的 `dsh-deepseek-usage`）升级

包名换了，dsh 会把它当成**两个不同的插件**，同时装会让界面出现两套余额栏。升级前先移除旧包：

```sh
npx @deepseek-ai/dsh plugin --profile desktop remove dsh-deepseek-usage
npx @deepseek-ai/dsh plugin --profile desktop add @blackthunder2191026/dsh-deepseek-usage
# 然后重启 dsh
```

### 所有方式都要做的一步

**重启 dsh。** 包 manifest、`exports`、profile 的 bundle 列表都不参与热重载；只改 `lib/client.js` 时刷新页面即可，改了 `lib/index.js`（host 半）就必须重启。

## 验证安装是否成功

```sh
# 1) 装之前：包结构自检，不需要 dsh 在运行
npm run verify

# 2) 装好后：profile 里应出现该 bundle，且路由可访问
curl "http://127.0.0.1:<你的端口>/deepseek-usage/summary?debug=1"
```

第 2 步应返回 `{"ok":true,...,"balance":{...}}`，带 `debug=1` 时还会给出折叠诊断（是否找到会话、读了多少事件、算出多少轮）。`debug.diagnostics.reason` 是 `ok` 就说明这条链是通的。

**`npm run verify` 包含三个彼此独立的检查**，都不依赖你的 profile，也不发起网络请求：

| 脚本 | 检查什么 |
|---|---|
| `tools/verify-client.mjs` | 浏览器半能加载、两个 slot 注册成功、展开明细按真实 payload 渲染（含表头、单价、空值占位） |
| `tools/verify-render.mjs` | 用桩路由 + 每实例一套 hook 状态的桩 React，断言两个座位在真实数据下渲染正确（金额、tokens、未计价轮次文案、`TurnLocation` 形状兼容） |
| `tools/verify-composition.mjs --source` | 复刻 dsh 的解析链：manifest 的 `dsh.client` / `exports["./client"]` / 产物里的模块 id / bundle patch 的行 id 三者一致 |

维护者另外还有一条 `npm run selfcheck`：发布前扫描所有文件，检查是否混入本机绝对路径、用户名、疑似密钥，以及 `repository`/`homepage`/`bugs`/`author` 等发布元数据是否齐全。

## 排错

| 现象 | 原因与处理 |
|---|---|
| 图形市场里点安装失败，提示「只能安装已发布到 npm 的插件」 | 该客户端只接受 `包名@精确版本`。用「安装」方式一（npm）或方式四（tarball）；若仍报错，是市场缓存了旧目录 |
| 界面上出现两套余额栏 | 旧的 `dsh-deepseek-usage` 与新的 `@blackthunder2191026/dsh-deepseek-usage` 同时装着。见「从旧版本升级」一节 |
| 侧边栏没有余额行 | 该 profile 没有 webserver 或不是 Web 界面；或 host 半未激活。先看 `?debug=1` 有没有响应 |
| 余额显示不可用 | 没有 `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`，或你用的不是官方 DeepSeek provider |
| 每轮只显示「本轮进行中，结束后计价」 | 该轮尚未结束（正常）；若显示「本轮未计价（宿主已算到第 N 轮）」则是异常，请反馈那一整行 |
| 启动时报 `declares no dsh.bundle` | 包没装全，或安装链接损坏；重新安装 |
| 安装时报 ENOENT 指向某 tgz | 你删掉了 profile 正在引用的 tarball；重新 `pnpm pack` 并按原路径放回，或重新安装 |
| 改了代码不生效 | host 半需重启 dsh；client 半需刷新页面（强刷 Ctrl+F5） |

## 维护者注：发布与续版

包名是 scope 形式（`@blackthunder2191026/dsh-deepseek-usage`），scope 不会与任何人冲突——npm 上无 scope 的 `dsh-deepseek-usage` 是无关项目，不能用那个名字。

```sh
npm login                     # 首次需浏览器认证
npm publish                   # publishConfig.access=public 已配置，scoped 包也会公开发布
```

**发布前必看**：`package.json` 的 `name`、`cordis.patch.yml` 里行的 `name`、`lib/client.js` 中 `__ModuleLoader__.load({ id })` 这三处必须是**同一个字符串**。任何一处不一致，要么插件根本不挂载，要么浏览器侧静默不加载（表现为侧边栏和对话底部都没有东西，且不报错）。`npm run selfcheck` 与 `npm run verify:package` 都会检查这一点。

续版流程：改 `version` → `npm run verify && npm run selfcheck` → `npm publish` → 打 tag 推 GitHub → 重新 `pnpm pack` 并把新 tgz 传到 Release。

## 计费口径

- 数据来自**会话日志里 provider 真实上报的 usage**（`assistant/message.usage`），不是界面上的估算值。
- 每轮按以下公式计价（价格单位：元 / 百万 tokens）：

  ```
  花费(CNY) = 未命中输入 × miss价
            + (缓存命中输入 + 缓存写入) × hit价
            + 输出 × output价
  ```

  价目表来自**官方中文定价页**（<https://api-docs.deepseek.com/zh-cn/quick_start/pricing/>），单位就是**元 / 百万 tokens**，与余额同币种。缓存写入按未命中价计。

  > 早期版本用的是**英文页的美元表**，再乘一个 `usdToCny`（我当时填 7.1）换成人民币。那是错的：中文页并不是英文页的固定换算——`0.02/0.003 = 6.6667`（Flash）而 `0.15/0.022 = 6.8182`（Pro），是**各自独立定价**。用 7.1 去折美元表，得到的数字官方两边都对不上（实测偏高约 6%）。现在直接采用中文页的元价，**插件里不再有任何汇率**。
- 高峰/低谷自动判断：高峰为**北京时间周一至周五 09:00–12:00 与 14:00–18:00**（即 01:00–04:00 与 06:00–10:00 UTC），其余时段（含周末）为低谷，费率为高峰的一半。中国法定节假日无法自动识别，那几天会按高峰计（偏高）。
- 花费与余额同为人民币，可直接相减；**没有任何汇率换算**。
- **只有已经结束的轮次才计价**（日志里 `turn/end` 已落盘）。进行中的这一轮显示「花费统计中…」，结束后自动出现金额。
- API Key 只在 Host 侧经 `ctx.credentials` 读取（`~/.dsh/.credentials.yaml` 的 `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`，或同名环境变量），**不会下发到浏览器**；浏览器只请求同源的 `/deepseek-usage/summary`。

## 关于本机 profile 的两点提醒

> **必须重启 dsh 进程**：包 manifest、`exports`、profile bundle 列表都不参与热重载；只有同一路径下 `lib/client.js` 内容变化（配 `tsdown --watch` 之类 watcher）才走 client HMR。
>
> **tarball 方式安装后别删那个 tgz**：profile 的 `package.json` 会用 `file:` 指向它，删了它 pnpm 下次安装会报 ENOENT。

## 改配置

行 id 是 `deepseek-usage`。改配置走 profile 的 `cordis.patch.yml` —— **整段替换，不是深合并**，要重述全部需要的键：

```yaml
- id: deepseek-usage
  name: dsh-deepseek-usage
  config:
    apiKeyEnv: DEEPSEEK_API_KEY   # 凭据引用名，同时作为环境变量名
    baseURL: https://api.deepseek.com
    currency: CNY                 # 余额币种；价目表也用这个币种，不做换算
    balanceTtlMs: 30000           # 余额缓存时长
    defaultModel: deepseek-flash  # 价目表里没有的模型用哪一行
    maxTurns: 300                 # 单次返回的最大轮次数
    models:                       # 元 / 百万 tokens（官方中文定价页）
      deepseek-flash:
        hit:    { peak: 0.04, offPeak: 0.02 }
        miss:   { peak: 2,    offPeak: 1 }
        output: { peak: 8,    offPeak: 4 }
      deepseek-v4-pro:
        hit:    { peak: 0.3,  offPeak: 0.15 }
        miss:   { peak: 9,    offPeak: 4.5 }
        output: { peak: 27,   offPeak: 13.5 }
```

价格随 DeepSeek 官方调整而变，请对照 <https://api-docs.deepseek.com/zh-cn/quick_start/pricing/> 更新 `models`。**注意别用英文页的美元价**——两页不是固定汇率关系。

## 实现结构

| 文件 | 作用 |
|---|---|
| `lib/index.js` | Host 半：`GET /user/balance` 取余额；按会话日志折叠每轮 token 并计价；注册 `GET /deepseek-usage/summary` |
| `lib/client.js` | 浏览器半：手写 `window.__ModuleLoader__.load` 工厂（无构建步骤），注册 `sidebar.footer.action` 与 `conversation.chat.turnTail` 两个 slot |
| `cordis.patch.yml` | bundle 层：插入 `deepseek-usage` 行并带默认配置与价目表 |
| `tools/verify-client.mjs` | 用假 loader / 假 cordis context 跑 client bundle：断言两个 slot 注册、首屏渲染，并把一份价格化的轮次推过展开明细 |
| `tools/verify-render.mjs` | 起一个桩 `/deepseek-usage/summary` 路由 + 每实例一套 hook 状态的桩 React，断言两个座位渲染出真实 payload（金额、tokens、未计价轮次文案） |
| `tools/verify-composition.mjs` | 复刻 `client-modules` 的解析链：profile bundle 列表 → Loader 解析归属 manifest → `dsh.client` 声明与 `./client` 产物 → `inject` 依赖可解析 → patch 行 id/name/config 与 host 导出一致 |
| `tools/verify-turns.mjs` | 解压真实 `.jsonl.zstd` 会话日志（多帧 zstd）并打印逐轮折叠结果 |

Host 半的每轮折叠是 `@deepseek-ai/dsh-token-meter` 里 `deriveTurnTokenUsage` 的等价实现，差别在于它保留每次 attempt 各自的 `provider/model` 路由，因此混合模型的会话也能逐轮正确计价。

## 自检

```sh

plugins.description: DeepSeek Harness plugin: turn a YouTube link into study notes — captions, on-screen content via vision, then your own notes merged in.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-youtube-study-notes

A [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (`dsh`) plugin that turns a YouTube link into study notes — and then gets *your* notes involved.

Give it a link. It pulls the video's own captions, samples the frames so it can read what was on screen, **stops and asks what you took from it**, and merges all three into one document.

The middle step is the point. Every other video-to-notes tool produces the same summary for everyone. This one writes the notes you'd have written, if you'd been taking notes.

## What it does

| Step | What happens |
|---|---|
| 1 | **Captions** — `yt-dlp` fetches the caption track YouTube already publishes. Human-written preferred, auto-generated as fallback. No ASR, no third-party transcript sites. |
| 2 | **Outline** — the timestamped transcript is read in full and outlined by chapter. |
| 3 | **Visual pass** *(optional)* — `ffmpeg` scene-change detection samples one frame per shot; a vision model reads the on-screen text. Catches slides, code, formulas and diagrams the narration never says out loud. |
| 4 | **Ask** — the agent stops and asks what *you* noticed, in your words. Type it or dictate it. |
| 5 | **Merge** — transcript + on-screen evidence + your observations, into one markdown file. |
| 6 | **Save** — `notes.md`, written beside the transcript so the evidence stays with it. |
| 7 | **Clean up** — the frame stills and any video file are removed; the transcript stays. |

### What it leaves on disk

The video is never kept: step 3 downloads it into a temporary directory that is deleted
when the script exits (`--keep-video` is the only way it survives). The frame JPEGs are
removed by step 7 once `notes.md` exists — they are derived from someone else's video and
are typically tens of megabytes, against a few kilobytes of transcript.

Kept, because it is the evidence behind every spoken claim and costs almost nothing:

```
transcript.md  transcript.txt  meta.json  notes.md
```

`cleanup.py` refuses to act on a directory that does not carry one of those markers, so
it cannot be pointed at an unrelated folder. Pass `--keep-frames` to review the stills
yourself.

## Install

```sh
dsh plugin --profile <your-profile> add dsh-youtube-study-notes
```

Restart the profile afterwards — bundle changes apply at boot.

Then trigger it either way:

```
/youtube-study-notes https://youtu.be/VIDEO_ID
```

or just ask in plain language ("get me notes from this video: …"). A link plus a request
for notes, a summary, or study material is enough.

> **Desktop clients:** the desktop app manages its own profile. Use its **Plugins → Add
> plugin** flow rather than the CLI, and enable the bundle when the install finishes.

## Requirements

The plugin ships no runtime code — its substance is the Skill, which drives local tools.
`dsh` does not install these for you:

| Tool | Role | Install |
|---|---|---|
| `python3` | runs the bundled scripts (standard library only) | `brew install python3` |
| `ffmpeg` / `ffprobe` | audio/video probing, scene detection, frame extraction | `brew install ffmpeg` |
| `yt-dlp` | caption listing and download | `brew install yt-dlp` |

The Skill detects missing tools, names them, and waits for your confirmation before
installing anything.

## Enabling the visual pass

Step 3 needs a model that accepts images, and **many model entries do not** — even ones
whose name says "vision". A model is only offered images if its configuration declares
`input: [text, image]`; entries otherwise default to `["text"]`, and the harness refuses
the image before attaching it with:

```
model "<provider>/<model>" does not declare image input
```

The Skill handles this: it tries `read_image` on a single frame first. If the session
model can see images, it reads the frames directly. If not, it delegates through the
`workflow` tool's per-agent `provider` / `model` override, and asks you once which
image-capable model to use.

To make a model explicitly image-capable, declare it in your profile's
`cordis.patch.yml` (the file your profile tells you to edit — not `cordis.yml`):

```yaml
- id: llm-pi-ai
  name: "@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm-pi-ai"
  config:
    providers:
      your-provider:
        # ...existing provider config...
        models:
          - id: "your-vision-model"
            name: "Your Vision Model"
            contextWindow: 200000
            input:
              - text
              - image
```

A profile with live reload picks this up without a restart.

> **Only declare this if the endpoint actually serves images.** Over-claiming admits an
> image the provider then rejects mid-turn, after the message is already durable. The
> declaration is not verified for you.

**If you skip all of this**, the plugin still works — it just produces transcript-only
notes, and says so rather than pretending it saw the screen.

## Limitations

- **Caption-less videos stop the run.** If a video publishes no caption track at all
  (not even auto-generated), step 1 reports which video failed and stops. Nothing is
  invented to fill the gap. Pair this with a local speech-to-text plugin if you need
  those covered.
- **Auto-generated captions are rough** — no punctuation, misheard proper nouns. The
  skill always reports which kind it got.
- **Vision reads can be wrong at the character level.** A period can read as a hyphen,
  `1` as `l`. Fine for prose, worth double-checking in code and formulas. The skill is
  instructed to flag anything load-bearing that looks ambiguous.
- **Frame sampling sees shots, not motion.** A diagram built up over one continuous shot
  yields a single frame.
- **Personal study use.** Captions, frames and notes are derived from someone else's
  work. Don't republish them.

## How it's built

```
package.json          declares dsh.bundle → cordis.patch.yml
cordis.patch.yml      inserts one @deepseek-ai/dsh-skill-filesystem row
lib/index.js          resolveSkillRoot() — resolves skills/ from the profile's own module identity
skills/youtube-study-notes/
  SKILL.md            the workflow
  scripts/            yt_transcript.py, video_frames.py, cleanup.py
  references/         notes template and merge rules
```

The bundle mounts its `skills/` directory as an **isolated** provider
(`includeDefaultRoots: false`), so installing it contributes exactly one skill and
cannot shadow or reorder the ones you already have.
